column1: # Serbian (sr) catalog, Latin script, Ekavian. Columns, separated by a TAB:  context <TAB> source <TAB> translation
#   context  empty                a plain UI string; `source` is the English text in the code
#            @id                  a command id (e.g. file.saveAs): wins over the English text for
#                                 that menu item, so one id can read differently from its twin
#                                 not 12–14 | everything else), see `plural` in i18n/mod.rs
#   escapes  \n  \t  \\  inside a column. `{name}` placeholders must appear in both columns.
#   lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored.
# Clean-room: every entry was written from the plain meaning of the English label using ordinary
# Serbian computing vocabulary (sloj, maska, selekcija, četkica, gradijent, zamućenje,
# neprozirnost, providnost ...). No proprietary localisation resource, string table or product UI
# was consulted or copied; in particular not the Serbian localisation of Adobe Photoshop. Add
# Conventions: Serbian Latin script (latinica), Ekavian (ekavica), sentence case. Menus are nouns
# (Datoteka, Uređivanje, Slika ...), commands are imperatives (Otvori…, Sačuvaj kao…), tools read
# "Alatka …" (Alatka četkica, Alatka za pomeranje), presets are "šabloni", patterns "šare" and
# swatches "uzorci boja". Serbian quotation marks „…“ around names. Product and technology names
# (PhotoCraft, ArtCraft, Camera Raw, OpenType, Lab ...) stay as they are; RGB/CMYK stay as they
# are; the trailing "…" of dialog commands is kept. A count that is not an @plural entry is kept
# out of noun agreement ("Broj: {n}", "slojeva: {n}") so every number reads correctly.
